Local proposed comparison bound: 2gamma2/(1-gamma2)*abs(native), gamma2=2u/(1-2u),u=eps/2.
Both size-one C and candidate Rust reciprocal/product paths use normal finite
operands. For weight3/10/100 specifically: squares9/100/10000 are exact;
GNU power-of-two denominator scaling remains exact and normal, scaled squares
and numerator1*scaledWc are exact; imaginary operands/products are zero.
Reciprocal division and final component multiply are the only nontrivial
roundings. This is NOT a generic complex-quotient gamma2 justification.
Let exact product q and each computed R,C have relative error <=gamma2.
Then |R-C|<=2gamma2*|q| and |q|<=|C|/(1-gamma2), giving stated cross-reference
factor. Test evaluates gamma2 upward, denominator downward, factor and final
bound upward using neighboring binary64 numbers. Nearby subtraction is exact
by Sterbenz; far-away unexpected values cannot pass the tiny bound.
This is an operation-local arithmetic bound, NOT Lanczos output tolerance or
ill-conditioned closed-form forward-error budget. Requires parent approval.
Order-specific regression separately checks SAME implementation multiplication
against divide for fixed literals, no cross-language computed-bit acceptance.
Modes0/1/2 in test are synthetic buffers, not public model-mode validation.
Fixture-only numeric comparison must not be confused with whole-model closure.
